263	/-- **The sheaf axiom of `picEt` at an arbitrary covering sieve.**
264	
265	This is `PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` (`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`) unfolded at
266	one sieve, and it is stated here to make the division of labour explicit: the
267	sheaf property is **free** — it is `PicSharp.etaleSheaf`'s own `Sheaf.cond`,
268	pushed through the forgetful functor — and holds at *every* covering sieve of
269	`etaleTopologyOver k`, the trivial sieve `⊤` included. Nothing about a field
270	extension enters.
271	
272	An earlier revision of this file proved the sheaf property again here, by a
273	different route (`Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget` in place of
274	`sheafCompose`), and presented it as new work. It was already in this file's
275	import closure; the duplicate is deleted rather than annotated. What §1–§3
276	contribute is not the sheaf axiom but a **particular covering sieve** that the
277	campaign's descent step needs and that the tree did not have. -/
278	theorem isSheafFor_picEt_of_mem (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
279	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
280	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (S : Sieve T)
281	    (hS : S ∈ etaleTopologyOver k T) :
282	    Presieve.IsSheafFor (PicScheme.picEt C) (S : Presieve T) :=
283	  PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget C S hS
284	
285	/-- **The sheaf axiom of `picEt` at the field-extension cover.**
286	
287	Concretely: for a `k`-scheme `T` and a finite separable `k'/k`, a family of
288	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}`-classes on `T ×_k k'` that is compatible on overlaps has a
289	*unique* amalgamation on `T`. No hypothesis on `C(k)` anywhere.
290	
291	**Where the content is, stated precisely because an earlier revision of this
292	docstring got it wrong.** That revision called this "THE DESCENT TEST" and "the
293	payoff", implying the sheaf side was the achievement. It is not: by
294	`isSheafFor_picEt_of_mem` the amalgamation property holds at *every* covering
295	sieve, `⊤` included, for free from sheafification. The only thing this
296	declaration adds over that is the *membership witness* — that this particular
297	family, the one the campaign's descent step actually restricts along, is a
298	covering sieve. That witness is §1–§3, and it is what the tree lacked.
299	
300	**What it does not give, and this is the larger half.** A descent *test* is not a
301	descended object. Turning a `k'`-representing scheme into a `k`-representing one
302	needs the semilinear Galois action and the effectivity of the resulting descent
303	datum — campaign `G1`/`G2`, `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`, whose existence
304	gate `HasGaloisQuotient` is discharged only for an **affine** total space
305	(`Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean`, 2026-07-30) while the object this route
306	descends is glued, so the gate still bites here. So this closes no `sorry` and
307	witnesses no antecedent of `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`. -/
308	theorem isSheafFor_picEt_pullback_presieve (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
309	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
310	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
311	    Presieve.IsSheafFor (PicScheme.picEt C)
312	      (((Sieve.overEquiv T).symm
313	        (Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton
314	          (pullback.fst T.hom
315	            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))))) : Presieve T) :=
316	  isSheafFor_picEt_of_mem C _ (sieve_pullback_mem_etaleTopologyOver k' T)
317	
318	/-- **The separatedness half, in the form `G3` uses it: restriction along the
319	cover is injective on `picEt`-classes.**
320	
321	Two classes in `Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that agree after restriction along the
322	base-changed field-extension cover are *equal*. This is the direction the
323	Hilbert-90 step of campaign `G3` consumes — it is what makes an invariant class
324	determined by its `k'`-shadow, so that a descent datum is unique once it exists.
325	
326	It is strictly weaker than `isSheafFor_picEt_pullback_presieve` (separatedness is
327	the uniqueness half of the sheaf axiom) and is recorded separately because it is
328	the half that is used on its own. The corresponding statement for `picSharp` is
329	*not* known to fail — `th:cmp` part 1 gives `picSharp ↪ Pic_{(C/k)zar}` on these
330	binders — so it is the *amalgamation* half above, not this one, that the repair
331	depends on. -/
332	theorem picEt_ext_of_pullback_agrees (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
333	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
334	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
335	    {t₁ t₂ : (PicScheme.picEt C).obj (Opposite.op T)}
336	    (h : ∀ ⦃W : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))⦄ ⦃g : W ⟶ T⦄,
337	      (((Sieve.overEquiv T).symm
338	        (Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton
339	          (pullback.fst T.hom
340	            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))))) : Presieve T) g →
341	      (PicScheme.picEt C).map g.op t₁ = (PicScheme.picEt C).map g.op t₂) :
342	    t₁ = t₂ :=
343	  (isSheafFor_picEt_pullback_presieve k' C T).isSeparatedFor.ext h

theorem smoothOfRelativeDimension_iff_pointwise_rank {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (n : ℕ) :
    SmoothOfRelativeDimension n f ↔
      ∀ x : X, ∃ (U : Y.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (V : X.Opens)
        (_ : IsAffineOpen V) (_ : x ∈ V) (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U),
        (f.appLE U V e).hom.IsStandardSmooth ∧
          (letI := (f.appLE U V e).hom.toAlgebra;
            Module.rank Γ(X, V) (Ω[Γ(X, V)⁄Γ(Y, U)]) = (n : Cardinal)) := by
  constructor
  · intro h x
    obtain ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hxV, e, hn⟩ := h.exists_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension x
    letI := (f.appLE U V e).hom.toAlgebra
    haveI : Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension n Γ(Y, U) Γ(X, V) := hn
    haveI : Nonempty (V : Type _) := ⟨⟨x, hxV⟩⟩
    haveI : Nontrivial Γ(X, V) := Scheme.component_nontrivial X V
    exact ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hxV, e,
      Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.isStandardSmooth (n := n),
      Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.rank_kaehlerDifferential n⟩
  · intro h
    refine ⟨fun x => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hxV, e, hss, hr⟩ := h x
    refine ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hxV, e, ?_⟩
    letI := (f.appLE U V e).hom.toAlgebra
    haveI : Algebra.IsStandardSmooth Γ(Y, U) Γ(X, V) := hss
    haveI : Nonempty (V : Type _) := ⟨⟨x, hxV⟩⟩
    haveI : Nontrivial Γ(X, V) := Scheme.component_nontrivial X V
    exact (Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.iff_of_isStandardSmooth
      (R := Γ(Y, U)) (S := Γ(X, V)) n).mpr hr

Unfolding a typeclass into chart language feels like a reduction and is not. Measured
2026-07-29 (AJC run 0084 r2, my own claim, refuted by a `work-reviewer` audit; I
reproduced the refutation before accepting).

The leaf was `SmoothOfRelativeDimension n f`. `HasRingHomProperty.iff_appLE` turns it
into a condition on affine chart pairs. I stated `.mpr` of that as a reduction with **no
smoothness hypothesis** and concluded "the leaf is one obligation, the smoothness half is
absorbed". Two defects:

- the hypothesis has no smoothness in it because `iff_appLE`'s right-hand side **is** the
  class. Nothing was absorbed. The absorption lemma I cited as the mechanism
  (`IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.isStandardSmooth`) was invoked by **no
  declaration in my own file** — `#print` on the theorem showed the body was exactly
  `(iff … ).mpr h`.
- the unfolded form was **harder** than the class. `SmoothOfRelativeDimension`'s field is
  *pointwise-existential* (`∀ x, ∃ U V affine, …`): one chart pair per point. The `iff`'s
  RHS demands the condition at *every* pair. So I pointed the next prover at more work
  than mathlib asks.

**How to apply:** before calling any `iff`-derived statement a reduction, `#print` the
theorem and read its body — if it is `.mpr` of an unfolding, say so in the docstring.
Then `#print` the **class** and compare quantifiers: if the class field is
`∀ x, ∃ …` and your hypothesis is `∀ …`, you have strengthened, not reduced. The honest
target is usually the anonymous constructor over the pointwise form.

Corollary I also got wrong in the same file: a failing `inferInstance` for a
`HasRingHomProperty` is not a mathematical absence — the proposition may be a library
`iff` ([[failing-inferinstance-is-not-absence]]). And an equality proved by one `rw` that
holds for an *arbitrary* property carries no content about the property you care about;
check genericity before drawing a conclusion from it, or you will dismiss a live route
(I dismissed homogeneity, which the pointwise field makes exactly the right route).
See also [[obligations-list-is-names-not-distances]].

    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]

    (α : A ⟶ B) (hα : η[A] ≫ α = η[B]) : IsMonHom α := by

  have : GeometricallyIrreducible A'.hom := by

    have hpt : η[A'] ≫ F.map α = η[B'] := by simp [← Functor.map_comp, hα]

Unfolding a typeclass into chart language feels like a reduction and is not. Measured
2026-07-29 (AJC run 0084 r2, my own claim, refuted by a `work-reviewer` audit; I
reproduced the refutation before accepting).

The leaf was `SmoothOfRelativeDimension n f`. `HasRingHomProperty.iff_appLE` turns it
into a condition on affine chart pairs. I stated `.mpr` of that as a reduction with **no
smoothness hypothesis** and concluded "the leaf is one obligation, the smoothness half is
absorbed". Two defects:

- the hypothesis has no smoothness in it because `iff_appLE`'s right-hand side **is** the
  class. Nothing was absorbed. The absorption lemma I cited as the mechanism
  (`IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.isStandardSmooth`) was invoked by **no
  declaration in my own file** — `#print` on the theorem showed the body was exactly
  `(iff … ).mpr h`.
- the unfolded form was **harder** than the class. `SmoothOfRelativeDimension`'s field is
  *pointwise-existential* (`∀ x, ∃ U V affine, …`): one chart pair per point. The `iff`'s
  RHS demands the condition at *every* pair. So I pointed the next prover at more work
  than mathlib asks.

**How to apply:** before calling any `iff`-derived statement a reduction, `#print` the
theorem and read its body — if it is `.mpr` of an unfolding, say so in the docstring.
Then `#print` the **class** and compare quantifiers: if the class field is
`∀ x, ∃ …` and your hypothesis is `∀ …`, you have strengthened, not reduced. The honest
target is usually the anonymous constructor over the pointwise form.

Corollary I also got wrong in the same file: a failing `inferInstance` for a
`HasRingHomProperty` is not a mathematical absence — the proposition may be a library
`iff` ([[failing-inferinstance-is-not-absence]]). And an equality proved by one `rw` that
holds for an *arbitrary* property carries no content about the property you care about;
check genericity before drawing a conclusion from it, or you will dismiss a live route
(I dismissed homogeneity, which the pointwise field makes exactly the right route).
See also [[obligations-list-is-names-not-distances]].

morphism, which is `quasiCompact` above, plus `ValuativeCriterion.Existence`, the

vocabulary — which matters, because mathlib v4.31 has none, and that absence is the

Through representability a `Spec R`-point of `Pic⁰` is a relative Picard class, so

Every other conjunct of `IsProper` is a theorem: `IsSeparated` is
`Pic0Et.isSeparated` (clopen immersion into the separated ambient `PicSchemeEt`),

étale tower, and its hypothesis is the only one mathlib has vocabulary for.

closedness of `Pic_{C/k}` is false, since it would force `CompactSpace` on an

HOW TO APPLY. When auditing, do not stop at 'is the statement true and non-vacuous'. Read the docstring for its own downgrade language and COUNT the downgraded declarations as zero. A file where the majority of decls carry a self-retraction is a churning file even though every individual line is defensible. And when writing: if you find yourself typing 'this is not a reduction' into a docstring, the correct move is to not add the declaration -- put the one-line fact at the consumer instead. The pair 'lemma + converse proving the lemma is empty' is two declarations of nothing.

Related: unfolded-class-is-not-a-reduction (same lane, one round earlier, same shape); caveat-passes-fix-the-weak-phrase; finish-it-instead-of-pricing-it."

Filed I-1282, I-1283 (issues) and I-1284 (memory).

## Findings

I read the statement of every new declaration in the ~20 files the four lanes added in the last 14 hours. **No vacuity of the `HasDivFunctor` kind exists in this round** — no binder that fails to occur in its body, no witness-discarding existential, no all-hypotheses-unused declaration, and no new `sorry` token. That failure mode is genuinely gone. What is wrong is different.

`Pic0Et.compactSpace` / `.specializingMap` / the four cover-transfer spellings — `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0EtProperImage.lean:136,161,213,228,261,275` — 7 of the file's 11 declarations are labelled by their own docstrings as renamings ("a convenience name for a triviality", "one transfer lemma and none is a reduction"), and the other 4 are the converses proving the 7 add nothing.

`leafB_of_chartwise`, `leafB_iff_appLE`, `leafB_of_pointwise` — `.../AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0EtRelativeDimension.lean:242,198,264` — respectively `iff_appLE.mpr`, mathlib's `HasRingHomProperty.iff_appLE`, and the class's anonymous constructor; the file admits all three, one round after the same lane was refuted for the same shape.

Whole `Pic0Et` tower (62 decls, 4 files) — `Pic0EtProperImage.lean:115`, `Pic0EtStructure.lean:174`, `Pic0EtTangentSpace.lean:139ff`, `Pic0EtRelativeDimension.lean:147` — every declaration binds `[HasPicSchemeEt C]`, whose unconditional instance is `(fgaPicardRepresentability C).1`, a projection of the seam `sorry` at `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:644`. Axiom-clean as implications, `sorryAx` at any real use site. Accurately documented, and unchanged by this round.

`uniformBaseDivisor_of_exists_deg_le` — `.../AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/Ledger/BaseDivisorEveryField.lean:214` — its hypothesis is definitionally `UniformBaseDivisor C d` and the body is `fun κ _ _ => h κ`; the file says so ("the IDENTITY, not even bookkeeping") and ships it anyway.

`PullbackTensorRightUnit` — `.../AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/PullbackTensorOneSided.lean:240` — a no-instance gate carrying the file's real residue. Sound as a pattern (`pullbackTensorRightUnit_of_iso_unit` exhibits a witness, so not vacuous), but `pullbackTensorIsoOfTwist:208` supersedes its main consumer unconditionally, so the gated pair below it is mostly dead weight.

`Scheme.DivFamily.*_pushforward` (4 new theorems) — `.../AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivPushforwardFlat.lean:205,254,272,299` — true theorems about `Scheme.DivFamily`, which the file itself records as having 135 consumers and zero producers in the project. Real content, about an uninhabited carrier.

Genuine throughput, gate-free and substantial: `PicEtCrossBase.lean`'s presheaf-level cross-base face assembled to `picEt_crossBaseIso` unconditionally (`:690`), `exists_isGaloisQuotient_of_isAffine` (`Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean:144`), `exists_finiteSeparable_level_factorization` (`Curve/FiniteLevelRationalPoint.lean:253`), and the p4 semicontinuity chain (`FiberRankSemicontinuity`, `TwoTermKernelSemicontinuity`, `PointRankSemicontinuity` + its witness), which is ordinary commutative algebra proved properly.

## Verdict

**Churning, with a real minority that will hold.** The three cross-base/Galois/finite-level files and the p4 semicontinuity chain are sound mathematics that will still be true and useful in a month. Against that, roughly 60% of the round's new declarations are either self-admitted renamings, iff-unfoldings, converse-pairs proving their siblings empty, or gate-bound statements about an object no curve inhabits — and of 73 commits, subjects beginning `docs(`/`fix(`/`retract(`/`board(` outnumber `feat(`. The seam `sorry` count is unchanged. The lanes have become excellent at documenting that their output adds nothing, which is precisely why no vacuity, sorry, or axiom check catches it.
